properties.statement: ON A SHARED GRAPH A WRITE'S OWN RESPONSE REPORTS WHAT WAS SENT, NOT WHAT PERSISTED — SAME-PROPERTY WRITES ARE SILENT LAST-WRITER-WINS AND THERE IS NO VERSION FIELD TO NOTICE IT WITH. Established by a deliberate experiment on the live 7-seat dev_storyflow graph (api-boss `5d608b85`, 2026-08-07, at the user's request), on a throwaway Requirement named to be unmistakable to the other attached sessions, with independent get_node read-backs after every write and the graph restored exactly afterwards (gap_count 69 -> 70 during -> 69 after, get_node -> null). TWO PROPERTIES HELD AND ARE WORTH RECORDING AS WON: per-property merge is real — writer B setting only `statement` left A's `rationale`, `name`, `priority`, `status` all intact, so two sessions editing different aspects of one node do not destroy each other; and concurrent writes SERIALIZE cleanly, with both racers' distinct properties surviving, no interleaving, no torn node, no error. THE DEFECT IS THE THIRD RESULT: when both racers wrote the SAME property, RACER_ONE's value was destroyed with no error, no warning, no version conflict, and no indication a value had been replaced — and RACER_ONE's own success payload read back `statement: RACER_ONE, priority: high` when the persisted state was already `RACER_TWO`/`low`. BOTH FIELDS IN THAT SUCCESS RESPONSE WERE FALSE WHEN IT WAS RETURNED. Why it is sharp rather than academic: on a solo graph response == state, so trusting your own write-response costs nothing and every habit formed under stdio does exactly that. Under `--shared` they diverge silently, and there is no `version`, `rev`, `etag` or `updated_at` anywhere in the payload — so a client cannot detect that it lost and has no primitive to compare-and-swap with. A session that writes a value and later reasons from its own return value is reasoning from something that was never durable. FIX SHAPE, from the reporter: return a monotonic `rev` per node and accept an optional `if_rev` on write; even unenforced, merely RETURNING it lets a caller notice it was superseded. Cheapest version: have the write response say 'this node was also written by another seat since your read.' BOUND THE REPORTER STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: the two racing writes were near-simultaneous requests from ONE MCP client process, not two OS-level sessions — the serialization and merge findings are server-side and hold regardless, but two distinct client processes were not proven and they do not claim it.
properties.value: {"reported":"2026-08-07 dev_storyflow, api-boss 5d608b85, deliberate experiment on the live shared graph","held":"per-property merge under concurrency; clean serialization; no torn state","defect":"same-property write is silent last-writer-wins AND the success payload reports the write, not the state","evidence":"RACER_ONE got success for statement=RACER_ONE, priority=high; persisted was RACER_TWO/low","missing_primitive":"no version/rev/etag/updated_at anywhere in the payload","fix_shape":"monotonic per-node rev returned on write, optional if_rev; minimum: say the node was written by another seat since your read","stated_bound":"two racers were one client process, not two OS sessions; server-side findings hold regardless","graph_restored":"yes, verified by control"}
